sampling_model.design: Known history-predictable randomization \(p_{bi}(z\mid H_{bi})\) on ordered enrollment positions.
sampling_model.units: The typed unit-level potential-outcome schedule encodes no cross-unit interference, the observation map \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{bi}=Y_{bi}(Z_{bi})\) encodes consistency, block membership is fixed, and assignment is the experiment's only endogenous randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: The shared control is available in every block, while the focal arm has positive propensity exactly on the proper block window \(W\).
sampling_model.overlap: The finite-horizon primitive requires positive propensity for every arm that is available at each compatible history and permits structural zeros for unavailable arms. This is an availability-restricted adaptation of the full-analyzed-arm positivity condition used by LiZhao2026, not a claim that their design class supplies the present converse. No numerical floor is fixed uniformly across sequences in the proved primitive-class result. The residual question separately fixes one common \(\underline p>0\) across the compared design family and is not used by any proved headline.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Outcome regressions \(m_{bi}(z)\) are bounded and predictable; validity does not require consistency of these regressions.
sampling_model.procedure_randomization: A schedule-independent Markov kernel may use an auxiliary \(U_{\mathrm{aux}}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) independent of the assignment experiment; coverage and expected length are computed under that same extended law. The concurrent-only subclass observes all assignment and realized propensity metadata but no outcome outside \(W\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The two-stage adding-arm simulations compare all-control and concurrent-only analyses under linear and step trends, and the stage-adjusted analysis is equivalent to concurrent-only analysis while linear adjustment can fail under nonlinear drift.

Equation (3) writes the two-period regression estimator as a concurrent-control mean plus a weighted nonconcurrent trend adjustment, and Section 3.1.2 gives unbiasedness under equal additive arm trends.

Theorem 3 gives the efficient influence function for the concurrent average treatment effect, and Section 6 finds no first-order doubly robust NCC efficiency gain when availability is deterministic in entry time.
Theorem 4 proves design-unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem for finite-population AIPW under adaptive randomization with positive propensity for every analyzed treatment.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 optimize honest confidence intervals through convex-class modulus and worst-case bias geometry in a Gaussian regression experiment.
Theorem 1 lower-bounds the expected length of every honest interval by a between-class Gaussian modulus and constructs constant-factor adaptive intervals over convex classes.
The paper selects data-adaptive external-control weights to keep estimated expected bias below a prespecified cap and reports bootstrap Wald inference under model-based assumptions.

Theorem 4 gives the minimax confidence-interval-length rate and an attaining upper construction in a Gaussian RCT-plus-observational model with bounded scalar confounding bias; Theorem 5 gives the adaptive-confidence-interval lower bound and impossibility.

Definitions 2.1--2.3 define a concurrently randomized cohort by a common allocation design, define nonconcurrent controls by membership outside that cohort, and distinguish contemporaneous controls by same-stage enrollment.

The paper compares categorical fixed-effect, mixed-effect, and spline calendar-time adjustments for platform-trial nonconcurrent controls through simulation-based type-I-error and power analysis, finding spline control for sufficiently smooth trends and period fixed effects most robust for arbitrary equal-across-arm trends.

body.tldr: For the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm effect, the exact cumulative-discrepancy program gives the sharp bounded-drift borrowing bias, and a finite convex program balances that bias against an assignment-law-averaged predictable-AIPW martingale envelope. The projected interval is uniformly design-honest and has worst-case expected length at most twice the clipped optimized radius. The all-kernel lower side is the optimized observed-law total-variation envelope \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\sup_{0\le\eta<1-2\alpha}(1-2\alpha-\eta)\Omega_{\mathcal D,\Gamma}(\eta)\), with the fixed \(\eta_\alpha\) bound as a corollary. A continuum of focal schedules sharing the masked-history restriction sharpens the computable certificate to \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\max_S2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\). This is an adaptive minimax sandwich, not a matching frontier: an explicit positive-per-experiment three-block sequence has \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha,n}^\star=2M\) and ratio at most \(2(1-\alpha/2)/\sqrt{n\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\). The fixed-common-floor comparison remains an unanswered, nondependent question.

project_justification.gap: Platform-control papers study parametric or semiparametric calendar adjustment through bias, type-I error, power, or superpopulation efficiency, while Gaussian convex-class work studies minimax expected length in nonadaptive observation experiments. Those cited classes do not transfer an adaptive randomization converse by inclusion. On the present primitive class, an \(\alpha\)-only comparison between every honest variable-length interval and the predictable inverse-propensity radius is false: the quantitative rare-history sequence refutes it despite positive propensities in every finite experiment. Its floors shrink, leaving the fixed-common-floor comparison genuinely open.
project_justification.niche: The note makes the adaptive assignment tree and fixed potential-outcome schedule explicit. It combines the sharp bounded-total-variation drift support function, an implementable predictable-AIPW upper interval, the optimized all-kernel observed-law total-variation lower envelope, a continuum common-restriction argument giving the exact finite-tree certificate \(2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\), and a quantitative rare-history obstruction. The residual fixed-floor question is isolated outside the proved dependency spine.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution is an adaptive minimax sandwich: the projected convex-program interval has worst-case expected length at most twice its clipped radius, while every schedule-independent randomized interval obeys the optimized observed-law modulus lower envelope and the sharper common-mass mask certificate. Uniform honesty over the continuum \(\tau_W=t\) spends only one \(\alpha\), and Tonelli integration turns that pointwise common-event requirement into expected length \(2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\). The explicit three-block inequality quantifies why the upper radius is not an unrestricted minimax equivalent. For the NCC package and ACTT-style calibration, the radius is a certified conservative design-based scale; constant-factor minimax calibration under one common propensity floor remains open and unused.

body.related_work: LeeWason2020, BofillRoigEtAl2022, and KrotkaEtAl2025TemporalDrift compare all-control and concurrent-only platform procedures under parametric calendar models through bias, type-I error, and power. MarschnerSchou2024 formalizes concurrent cohorts, and SantacatterinaEtAl2025 studies superpopulation efficiency for a concurrent estimand. These works motivate the platform setting but do not give uniform fixed-schedule coverage over the present total-variation drift class. LiZhao2026 supplies the predictable-AIPW martingale template and positivity for every analyzed treatment; the present finite-horizon condition adapts positivity to available arms and permits structural support zeros off the focal window. ChenLiZhangYe2025, ArmstrongKolesar2018, and CaiLow2004 supply Gaussian bias--variance or modulus analogies. Their nonadaptive experiment classes do not transfer a converse here by inclusion once observed outcomes change later propensities. The proved lower result is instead an observed-law total-variation envelope under the actual adaptive assignment law, sharpened by a continuum of fixed focal schedules whose extended laws share the masked-event restriction; integrating their common-event coverage yields the one-\(\alpha\) positive part. The quantitative rare-history sequence rules out an \(\alpha\)-only comparison with the AIPW radius on the primitive class. Whether a fixed-common-floor subclass admits a constant depending on \(\alpha\) and that floor remains open and unused. SawadaNomuraShinozaki2026 concerns estimated bias caps and bootstrap inference under a different estimand and model, while AronowLopatto2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 do not combine staggered availability, bounded calendar drift, and adaptive-history masking.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The optimized predictable-AIPW radius is a valid constructive upper scale but is not the unrestricted minimax expected-length scale. The quantitative counterexample exploits an \(\alpha/2\)-probability branch whose focal propensity is \(\alpha/(2n)\): the second-moment radius clips at \(2M\), whereas an honest variable-length interval has ratio at most \(2(1-\alpha/2)/\sqrt{n\alpha/(2-\alpha)}\). Every experiment is positive, but the floor decreases with \(n\). Fixing one floor across a design family removes this witness without making outcome-adaptive assignment likelihoods comparable; schedule-supported fuzzy priors with a uniform sequential likelihood-ratio bound remain unavailable. The sharper continuum certificate \(\max_S2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\) is computable but is not asserted to be a necessary characterization of the full modulus. The vacuous-drift reduction still requires structural invariance of propensity updates to off-window potential-outcome changes.
body.honest_scope: The causal target is the window-weighted finite-population focal-arm-versus-control contrast, and assignment is the experiment's only source of randomness. The projected AIPW interval is uniformly honest under the primitive support, boundedness, and drift conditions without regression consistency or an assumed limit law. Every schedule-independent auxiliary-randomized variable-length observed-data interval obeys the optimized observed-law total-variation lower envelope and the sharper finite-tree certificate \(\mathfrak L_\alpha^\star\ge\max_S2Mw(S)[q_S-\alpha]_+\); the proof uses a continuum of admissible fixed schedules and a common extended-law restriction, not a superpopulation model. No universal \(\alpha\)-only equivalence with the optimized AIPW radius is claimed; the explicit three-block rate refutes it while retaining positivity in each experiment. Because that sequence has shrinking floors, the sole residual converse question fixes a common \(\underline p>0\) and allows its constant to depend on that floor; it is open and absent from the proved dependency closure. Comparator results are templates or analogies, not class-inclusion converses. The KKT result concerns AIPW radii. Zero drift leaves information-optimal borrowing, while the vacuous-drift all-kernel equality requires structural invariance of propensity updates to off-window potential-outcome changes. No claim is made that the drift budget is learned, that the mask certificate is necessary, or that the fixed-floor question is solved.
